subject: Coloring points by group in PCoA

messages.author: 04e71feb5b4997db
messages.subject: Coloring points by group in PCoA
parts:
Hello,

Does anyone know if there is a way to color the points in an interactive PCoA by a specific group? For example, I'd like the points in my interactive PCoA to be colored by species. Here is my code if necessary:

pcoa_interactive2 <- gl.pcoa.plot(pcoa2, gl2_complete, labels="interactive", xaxis=1, yaxis=2)
ggplotly()

Thanks for your help!
Dallas

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Coloring points by group in PCoA
parts:
Hi Dallas,

Could you please try the code below.

Please let us know whether it worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis

library(plotly)
gl <- testset.gl
# you could for example add the name of your species for each individual in the slot
# other$ind.metrics
# first how many individuals are there
number_individuals <- nInd(gl)
# setting half of individuals to be from species_1 and half for species_2
gl$other$ind.metrics$species <- c(rep("species_1",number_individuals/2),rep("species_2",number_individuals/2))
# The interactive plot uses individual names to fill the points and the population names
# for the borders of the points. So, if you want one color for each species, you can
# set the individual names and the populations names with the name of the species
# as follows
# setting species as individual names
indNames(gl) <- gl$other$ind.metrics$species
# setting species as population names
pop(gl) <- gl$other$ind.metrics$species
pca <- gl.pcoa(gl)
pcoa_interactive2 <- gl.pcoa.plot(pca, gl, labels="interactive", xaxis=1, yaxis=2,verbose=5)

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Re: Coloring points by group in PCoA
parts:
Hi Dallas,

I had a look at the challenge of allowing users to specify the sizes, shapes and colours of the points in the pcoa plots, but it is not as easy as one might think to implement. So I think it needs to go on the backburner. You have a couple of options.

(a) Save it as a vector file, and edit in illustrator
(b) Access the ggplot file (saved in dartR version 2) and use R to adjust the point shapes, colours and sizes.

Sorry I cannot be of more help at this time. We have been keen to have dartR deal with the computational side of things, and providing a conduit between SNP data and other applications, and have not devoted much time to the quality of graphics.

Arthur
